user_prompt: Write a polite but direct email contesting my late fee. I paid on time, the lease says so, and I want the charge removed from my account.
final_prompt:
Write a polite but direct email contesting my late fee. I paid on time, the lease says so, and I want the charge removed from my account.

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

runs.answer:
Dana's late fee doesn't hold up under your lease. Section 4.2 gives a grace period through the 5th and says no late fees may be charged during it. Your rent arrived on the 3rd, so the $75 charge violates the lease. Dana's email also doesn't mention a payment date that falls outside that window.

Here's a message you can send. Email counts as written notice under Section 9.4.

---

Subject: Request to reverse late fee – Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

I'm writing about the $75 late fee added to my account for this month. My rent payment was received on the 3rd, which falls within the grace period in Section 4.2 of my lease. That section states that no late fees may be charged during the grace period.

Please reverse the $75 charge and confirm in writing once it has been removed from my account. Please send the confirmation by [date, e.g., 7 days from today].

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

Some practical notes:

- Keep your proof of payment (bank statement, receipt, or portal confirmation showing the 3rd).
- Don't pay the $75 along with next month's rent. If you do, the lease says nothing about how they'd apply it, and it's harder to dispute later. If the fee is still on your account at the next billing, say so in writing.
- If they refuse, check your state or local tenant rules. Many places allow a tenant to recover the improper fee, and some have small claims or tenant-rights agencies that handle this kind of dispute cheaply.

Your lease is on your side here. Section 4.2 gives a grace period through the 5th, and it explicitly says no late fees may be charged during that period. Dana's email says your rent arrived on the 3rd, so the $75 charge conflicts with the lease.

Here's a reply you could send by email, which Section 9.4 allows:

---

Subject: Request to remove late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your email. My records show rent was received on the 3rd, which is within the grace period under Section 4.2 of my lease. That section states that no late fees may be charged during the grace period.

Please remove the $75 late fee from my account. If you have payment records showing a different date, please send them so I can review them.

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

Before sending, it's worth checking your payment confirmation for the date the payment posted or was submitted, in case the portal shows something different from the 3rd. Keep a copy of your reply and of the lease.

If they refuse, you can escalate in writing, and depending on where you live, your local tenant rights office or a housing attorney can help. Many areas also have small claims court for recovering improper fees.
